data_description.grid_power_max: Most your grid connection can import or export, set by your main fuse. Not the inverter rating: the house alone can draw more than that.
data_description.scan_interval: How often values are polled (2-30 seconds)
data_description.calc_solar_power: In some inverters, the modbus register delivers 0W of solar power. This switch allows the solar power to be calculated from the individual powers of the string.
data_description.battery_reserve: Native: the inverter enforces the reserve itself, like the one set in the EcoFlow app, but not every model accepts a change to it over Modbus. Emulated: the integration imitates the app's reserve with its own logic, while Modbus Control is on. Set for your model; change it only to test a model.
data_description.mqtt: Additionally connects to the EcoFlow cloud like the EcoFlow app (MQTT) and reads the firmware of the modules. The values still come from the regular polling.
data_description.live_power: Asks the system for its power values every 20 s, as the EcoFlow app does while it is open. Solar and the energy flows then update every ~5 s; house, grid and battery power too, while Modbus has no current reading. Only with the extended connection (MQTT).
data_description.max_schedule_power: Highest power in W that a schedule may use. Without a value, schedules cannot be added or changed. Only with the extended connection (MQTT).
data_description.calc_grid_energy: In some inverters, the grid import and export registers stay at 0 while Grid Power reads right. This switch calculates grid import and export from Grid Power instead. An estimate: it can differ from your meter by a few percent.
data_description.alert_verbosity: How much the integration raises in Settings → Repairs. Essential: only what you must act on, such as an inverter that stopped updating. Readings: also readings that cannot be trusted. Detailed: also the connection's health, such as frequent reconnects or late polls. Debug: also every warning and error the integration logs. Each alert can be ignored. Setting it back to Essential forgets the ignored alerts.

energy_totals.name: Correct energy totals
energy_totals.description: Only needed if the inverter reset one of its lifetime energy counters. Enter the value from EcoFlow's portal for each total that is wrong and leave the others as they are.

data.remove_corrections: Reset all totals to the inverter's values

data_description.remove_corrections: Removes every correction, so each total shows what the inverter reports. The values above are ignored.

error.invalid_energy_total: Enter each energy total as a number, with a comma or a point for decimals and without thousands separators.
error.energy_total_lowered: This would lower a total. Home Assistant records a drop as negative energy, or, if it is more than 10%, as a new meter that adds the whole value to the Energy dashboard. Check the values, then submit again to save them anyway. You can correct the history afterwards under Developer tools → Statistics → Adjust sum.

identity_mismatch.title: A different inverter answers at {host}
identity_mismatch.description: This entry belongs to the inverter with serial number {expected}, but the device at {host} reports {found}. Nothing is read from or written to it, so Modbus control cannot be handed to an inverter you did not set up. Check that the address still points at the right inverter (a reserved address in your router prevents this), or remove this entry and add the new inverter.

modbus_disabled.title: Modbus is disabled on the inverter at {host}
modbus_disabled.description: The integration requires Modbus TCP to be enabled in the EcoFlow Pro app. Ask your installer to enable it and the integration will automatically start working.

not_answering_unreachable.title: The inverter at {host} is not reachable
not_answering_unreachable.description: Nothing has answered on the inverter's Modbus port since {since}. Check that the inverter is powered and still has the IP address {host}, for example in your router. In a few cases, a firmware update has also switched Modbus TCP off: if the inverter updated recently, ask your installer to enable it again in the EcoFlow Pro app. Its Modbus readings stay unavailable until it answers again, with the EcoFlow cloud's values standing in where the cloud is connected. This message then disappears by itself.

not_answering_modbus_silent.title: The inverter at {host} stopped answering Modbus
not_answering_modbus_silent.description: Since {since} the inverter takes connections on its Modbus port but sends no replies. In a few cases, a firmware update has switched Modbus TCP off: if the inverter updated recently, ask your installer to enable it again in the EcoFlow Pro app. Where the EcoFlow cloud is connected, its values stand in meanwhile. The integration recovers by itself once the inverter answers, and this message then disappears.

energy_totals_held.title: Energy totals of the inverter at {host} have been held for over a day

init.title: Energy totals held for over a day
init.description:
These lifetime energy totals have been held for more than 24 hours, because the inverter reports a value the integration does not consider plausible:

{totals}

This usually means the inverter reset its counter, or a wrong value was accepted earlier.

**Keep Home Assistant's totals** if the inverter reset its counter. Each total stays at its value in Home Assistant and counts on from there: the difference to the inverter is added to every reading from now on, and the Energy dashboard continues without a jump. You can match the totals to EcoFlow's portal later under the integration's [settings]({settings_page}): choose Configure, and on the second page open Correct energy totals.

**Switch to the inverter's totals** sets each total to the inverter's value and counts on from there. The Energy dashboard records the difference in one step. If the inverter's value is lower, Home Assistant records the drop as negative energy, or, if it is more than 10% lower, as a new meter that adds the whole value. You can correct the history afterwards under Developer tools → Statistics → Adjust sum.

If you believe these values are wrong, choose neither. Instead, open the inverter's [device page]({device_page}), choose **Download diagnostics** from its ⋮ menu, and attach the file to this [bug report]({report_url}), which is already filled in.

abort.not_held: These energy totals are no longer held.

grid_energy_not_counted.title: Grid energy of the inverter at {host} is not counted

confirm.title: Calculate grid energy from Grid Power
confirm.description:
For more than a day, the inverter has reported 0 for grid import and export, while Grid Power showed energy flowing through the grid. Grid Import, Grid Export and House Consumption therefore stay wrong.

Submit to calculate grid import and export from Grid Power instead. The totals continue from their current values, so the Energy dashboard records no jump. The calculation is an estimate: it can differ from your meter by a few percent, and energy is not counted while the inverter cannot be read. The (Device) sensors keep showing what the inverter reports.

You can turn this off again under the integration's [settings]({settings_page}): choose Configure and switch off Calculation of grid energy.

abort.not_needed: The grid energy registers are counting again, or grid energy is already calculated.

telemetry_stalled.title: The inverter at {host} stopped updating its readings
telemetry_stalled.description: The inverter still answers, but most of its readings haven't changed since at least {since}. Readings that stand still show as unavailable, or the EcoFlow cloud's values where the cloud is connected, and Modbus Control, if on, leaves the inverter to its own logic. Restart the inverter according to its manual. This issue goes away once the readings move again. If it keeps coming back, report it with the integration's diagnostics and the inverter's firmware version.

set_battery_command.name: Set battery command
set_battery_command.description: Sets the Battery Mode, its power and the Charge Limit in one step, optionally for a limited time. Meant for automations and battery planners.

power.name: Power
power.description: Power for the mode, above 0 W. Required for Charge battery, Discharge battery, Export to grid and Import from grid. Optional for Export solar first, where it sets the Solar Export Limit and leaving it out keeps the current one. Not allowed for the others. A value above what the inverter accepts is lowered to its maximum.

charge_limit_soc.name: Charge limit
charge_limit_soc.description: Sets the Charge Limit. Left as it is when omitted. The integration never changes it back by itself.

expire_in.name: Expire in
expire_in.description: Seconds until the mode returns to Automatic. Sending the command again starts the count over. Without it the mode stays until it is changed.

run_control_test.name: Run control test
run_control_test.description: Checks which control methods this inverter's firmware follows, and writes a report to attach to a GitHub issue. If Modbus Control is on, the selected battery mode pauses for the test and resumes after it. The battery charges and discharges briefly at the test power, and the inverter is handed back to the EcoFlow app at the end. Takes about 10 minutes. The action returns at once; the Control Test sensor follows the run, and a notification says when the report is ready.

confirm.name: Confirm
confirm.description: Must be on. The test writes control commands and pauses any selected battery mode, so the battery charges and discharges and power flows to and from the grid for a few minutes.

power.name: Test power
power.description: Power to command each method at, 600 to 3000 W. Lowered where the export cap allows less.

cancel_control_test.name: Cancel control test
cancel_control_test.description: Stops a running control test. The inverter is returned to the default method and handed back to the EcoFlow app.

device_id.name: Inverter
device_id.description: The inverter whose test to stop.

add_schedule.name: Add schedule
add_schedule.description: Adds a scheduled task to the inverter, as in the EcoFlow app. Needs "Max schedule power (W)" in the options. Choose the inverter in the Device field.

device_id.name: Device
device_id.description: The inverter to add the schedule to.

start.description: Start time, in steps of 30 minutes.

end.name: End

update_schedule.name: Update schedule
update_schedule.description: Changes a scheduled task: choose its switch as the target. What you leave empty stays as it is. Needs "Max schedule power (W)" in the options.

schedule_not_confirmed.message: The system acknowledged the command, but its list does not show the change yet. Check the app before you try again.
